for fork in range(1,forks+1):

event_only.jsonfuseddifferentialtest.lua:
-- The AOT fused JSON decoder and the Lunajson provider are two independent
-- readings of the same grammar: one scans with vectors and walks a structural
-- tape, the other is a third-party byte-at-a-time parser Nupp did not write.
-- Where they agree on a corpus they agree because both read JSON, not because
-- one was derived from the other.
--
-- The scan itself is checked a second way, against `referenceScan` below. That
-- is this file's independent scalar reference in the sense
-- `bench/simd-json/src/simd_json/indexer_reference.nupp` is the vector
-- indexer's: it shares no mask, no lane and no tape with the decoder, and it
-- states the same contract -- the first error in byte order, and the one-based
-- position of the byte that raised it.
--
-- Nothing here builds anything. With no linked artifact the `@aot` body runs
-- as ordinary Nupp, which is the same source and the same answers; what it
-- does not exercise is the emitted C, which the `aot` group covers. Every
-- literal below is ASCII, so a byte sequence under test is written as an
-- escape and never as itself.

local fused = require("nupp.codec.json.aot")
local lunajson = require("nupp.runtime.provider.lunajson")

local M = {}

local NULL = setmetatable({}, {__tostring = function() return "null" end})

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The shared corpus
----------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Documents both decoders must accept and agree on.
local WELL_FORMED = {
    -- Scalars and the whitespace around them.
    "0", "-0", "1", "-1", "123456789", "  42  ", "\t\r\n7\n", "true", "false", "null",
    '""', '"a"', '"hello world"',

    -- Numbers at and around the edges of binary64.
    "1e308", "-1e308", "1.7976931348623157e308", "-1.7976931348623157e308",
    "5e-324", "-5e-324", "2.2250738585072014e-308", "1e-323",
    "9007199254740991", "9007199254740992", "-9007199254740991",
    "0.1", "0.2", "0.30000000000000004", "1e-7", "1E+7", "1e0", "-0.0",
    "123456789012345678901234567890", "0.000000000000000000001",
    "1.000000000000000000000000000000001", "3.141592653589793",

    -- Containers, nesting and mixed shapes.
    "[]", "{}", "[[]]", "[{}]", '{"a":{}}', "[1,2,3]", "[1,[2,[3,[4]]]]",
    '{"a":1,"b":2,"c":3}', '{"a":[1,2],"b":{"c":[3]}}',
    '[null,true,false,0,"",[],{}]',
    '{"":1}', '{"a":null,"b":null}',
    "[ 1 , 2 , 3 ]", '{ "a" : 1 }',
    '{"a":[{"b":[{"c":[{"d":1}]}]}]}',

    -- Escapes, including every simple one and the pair a supplementary
    -- codepoint needs. These are long strings, so a backslash here is the
    -- backslash the decoder sees.
    [["\""]], [["\\"]], [["\/"]], [["\b"]], [["\f"]], [["\n"]], [["\r"]], [["\t"]],
    [["\u0041"]], [["\u00e9"]], [["\u0020"]], [["\u0001"]], [["\u001f"]],
    [["\u00ff"]], [["\u0800"]], [["\uffff"]], [["\ud83d\ude00"]], [["\udbff\udfff"]],
    [["a\\b"]], [["a\\\\b"]], [["\\\""]], [["\\\\\""]], [["a\nb\tc"]],
    [["\u0041\u0042\u0043"]],
    [[{"k\"ey":"v\\alue"}]],
    [[{"\u0041":"\u00e9"}]],

    -- Literal UTF-8 of every scalar length, written as byte escapes.
    '"\195\169"', '"\226\130\172"', '"\240\159\152\128"',
    '"\194\128"', '"\223\191"', '"\224\160\128"', '"\239\191\191"',
    '"\240\144\128\128"', '"\244\143\191\191"',
    '{"\226\130\172":"\240\159\152\128"}',
}

-- Inputs neither decoder may accept.
local MALFORMED = {
    "", "   ", "\n",
    "tru", "fals", "nul", "trues", "True", "NULL",
    "+1", "01", "-", "1.", ".1", "1e", "1e+", "--1", "1.2.3", "Infinity", "NaN",
    "[", "]", "{", "}", "[1", '{"a"', '{"a":', '{"a":1', "[1,", "[1,]", "{,}", "[,]",
    '{"a":1,}', '{"a" 1}', "{a:1}", "{'a':1}", "[1 2]", '{"a":1"b":2}',
    '"unterminated', '"a\\"', '"\\"', '"\\q"', '"\\u"', '"\\u12"', '"\\uZZZZ"',
    [["\ud800"]], [["\udc00"]], [["\ud800\ud800"]], [["\ud800x"]],
    "[1,2,3]extra", "{} {}", "1 2", "null null",
    -- Control bytes are never literal inside a string.
    '"\001"', '"\009"', '"\010"', '"\031"',
    -- A backslash outside a string is not a token.
    "[\\]", "\\", '{"a":\\}',
    -- Malformed UTF-8 of every failing shape.
    '"\128"', '"\191"', '"\192\128"', '"\193\191"', '"\194"', '"\224\128\128"',
    '"\224\159\191"', '"\237\160\128"', '"\240\128\128\128"', '"\244\144\128\128"',
    '"\245\128\128\128"', '"\255"', '"\226\130"', '"\240\159\152"',
    '\226\130\172', '"a\128b"',
}

-- Deep containers, built rather than written out.
local function nested(open, close, depth)
    return string.rep(open, depth) .. "1" .. string.rep(close, depth)
end

local function wideArray(count)
    local parts = {}
    for i = 1, count do
        parts[i] = tostring(i)
    end

    return "[" .. table.concat(parts, ",") .. "]"
end

local function wideObject(count)
    local parts = {}
    for i = 1, count do
        parts[i] = string.format('"k%d":%d', i, i)
    end

    return "{" .. table.concat(parts, ",") .. "}"
end

local function corpus()
    local all = {}
    for _, text in ipairs(WELL_FORMED) do
        all[#all + 1] = text
    end
    for depth = 1, 24 do
        all[#all + 1] = nested("[", "]", depth)
    end
    for _, count in ipairs({1, 2, 3, 15, 16, 17, 31, 32, 33, 63, 64, 65, 200}) do
        all[#all + 1] = wideArray(count)
        all[#all + 1] = wideObject(count)
    end
    -- Strings that straddle every plausible vector and block boundary, plain
    -- and escaped, so the whole-vector path and the byte-at-a-time tail both
    -- cover every shape at least once.
    for length = 0, 80 do
        all[#all + 1] = '"' .. string.rep("a", length) .. '"'
        all[#all + 1] = '["' .. string.rep("a", length) .. '","b"]'
        all[#all + 1] = '"' .. string.rep("\\n", length) .. '"'
        all[#all + 1] = '"' .. string.rep("a", length) .. '\\u00e9"'
        all[#all + 1] = '{"' .. string.rep("k", length) .. '":1}'
        all[#all + 1] = string.rep(" ", length) .. "[1]"
        all[#all + 1] = '"' .. string.rep("\226\130\172", length) .. '"'
    end
    -- Backslash runs of every parity across a vector boundary.
    for slashes = 1, 40 do
        all[#all + 1] = '"' .. string.rep("\\", slashes * 2) .. '"'
        all[#all + 1] = '"' .. string.rep("a", slashes) .. '\\\\"'
    end

    return all
end

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The independent scalar reference for the structural scan
----------------------------------------------------------------------------

local OK, INVALID_UTF8, INVALID_CONTROL, INVALID_BACKSLASH = 0, 2, 3, 4

-- Reads `source` one byte after another and keeps what a JSON structural scan
-- needs: whether it is inside a string, the parity of the backslash run before
-- the current byte, and for UTF-8 how many continuation bytes the last lead
-- still owes and what range the first of them must fall in.
--
-- Answers the first scan error in byte order as a code and the one-based
-- position of the byte that raised it, or `OK, 0`. A UTF-8 scalar the end of
-- the input cut off is raised one past the last byte. It says nothing about
-- the grammar above the bytes; that is what the decoders are compared on.
local function referenceScan(source)
    local inString, slashRun = false, 0
    local owed, constraint, lastNonAscii = 0, 0, -1

    for offset = 0, #source - 1 do
        local byte = source:byte(offset + 1)
        if owed > 0 then
            local continuation = byte >= 128 and byte <= 191
            local outside = constraint == 1 and byte < 160
                or constraint == 2 and byte > 159
                or constraint == 3 and byte < 144
                or constraint == 4 and byte > 143
            if not continuation or outside then
                return INVALID_UTF8, offset + 1
            end
            owed, constraint, lastNonAscii, slashRun = owed - 1, 0, offset, 0
        elseif byte >= 128 then
            if byte < 194 or byte > 244 then
                return INVALID_UTF8, offset + 1
            elseif byte <= 223 then
                owed = 1
            elseif byte <= 239 then
                owed = 2
                if byte == 224 then
                    constraint = 1
                elseif byte == 237 then
                    constraint = 2
                end
            else
                owed = 3
                if byte == 240 then
                    constraint = 3
                elseif byte == 244 then
                    constraint = 4
                end
            end
            lastNonAscii, slashRun = offset, 0
        elseif byte == 92 then
            if not inString then
                return INVALID_BACKSLASH, offset + 1
            end
            slashRun = slashRun + 1
        else
            local escaped = slashRun % 2 == 1
            slashRun = 0
            if byte == 34 and not escaped then
                inString = not inString
            elseif byte < 32 then
                if inString or not (byte == 9 or byte == 10 or byte == 13) then
                    return INVALID_CONTROL, offset + 1
                end
            end
        end
    end

    if owed > 0 then
        return INVALID_UTF8, lastNonAscii + 2
    end

    return OK, 0
end

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Comparison
----------------------------------------------------------------------------

local function render(value, seen)
    local kind = type(value)
    if value == NULL then
        return "null"
    elseif kind ~= "table" then
        if kind == "number" then
            return string.format("%.17g", value)
        end

        return kind .. ":" .. tostring(value)
    end
    seen = seen or {}
    assert(not seen[value], "the decoded value is cyclic")
    seen[value] = true
    local keys = {}
    for key in pairs(value) do
        keys[#keys + 1] = key
    end
    local array = true
    for index = 1, #keys do
        if value[index] == nil then
            array = false
            break
        end
    end
    local parts = {}
    if array then
        for index = 1, #keys do
            parts[index] = render(value[index], seen)
        end
        seen[value] = nil

        return "[" .. table.concat(parts, ",") .. "]"
    end
    table.sort(keys, function(left, right) return tostring(left) < tostring(right) end)
    for index, key in ipairs(keys) do
        parts[index] = string.format("%q", tostring(key)) .. ":" .. render(value[key], seen)
    end
    seen[value] = nil

    return "{" .. table.concat(parts, ",") .. "}"
end

local function decodedBy(provider, text)
    local ok, value = pcall(provider.decode, text, NULL)
    if not ok then
        return nil, tostring(value)
    end

    return render(value), nil
end

local function show(text)
    return (text:gsub("[^\032-\126]", function(c)
        return string.format("<%d>", c:byte())
    end)):sub(1, 60)
end

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The checks
----------------------------------------------------------------------------

function M.theFusedDecoderDecodesEveryCorpusDocumentAsLunajsonDoes()
    local checked = 0
    for _, text in ipairs(corpus()) do
        local mine, myError = decodedBy(fused, text)
        local theirs, theirError = decodedBy(lunajson, text)
        assert(
            myError == nil and theirError == nil,
            string.format(
                "%s should be well formed for both: fused=%s lunajson=%s",
                show(text),
                tostring(myError),
                tostring(theirError)
            )
        )
        assert(mine == theirs, string.format("%s decodes to %s but lunajson says %s", show(text), mine, theirs))
        checked = checked + 1
    end
    assert(checked > 700, "the corpus shrank to " .. checked .. " documents")
end

function M.theFusedDecoderRejectsEveryDocumentLunajsonRejects()
    for _, text in ipairs(MALFORMED) do
        local mine, myError = decodedBy(fused, text)
        local theirs, theirError = decodedBy(lunajson, text)
        assert(myError ~= nil, string.format("%s decoded to %s but is malformed", show(text), tostring(mine)))
        assert(
            theirError ~= nil,
            string.format("lunajson accepted the malformed %s as %s", show(text), tostring(theirs))
        )
    end
end

function M.theFusedScanReportsTheSameFirstErrorAsTheScalarReference()
    local checked = 0
    for _, text in ipairs(MALFORMED) do
        local code, position = referenceScan(text)
        if code ~= OK then
            local _, message = decodedBy(fused, text)
            assert(message ~= nil, string.format("%s decoded, but the reference raises %d at %d", show(text), code, position))
            local reported = tonumber(message:match("at byte (%d+)"))
            assert(reported ~= nil, string.format("%s reported %q, which names no byte", show(text), message))
            assert(
                reported == position,
                string.format("%s raises at byte %d but the reference says %d", show(text), reported, position)
            )
            checked = checked + 1
        end
    end
    assert(checked > 20, "the reference agreed on only " .. checked .. " inputs")
end

-- Malformed byte sequences on their own, to be placed at a chosen offset.
local BAD_UTF8 = {
    "\128", "\191", "\192\128", "\193\191", "\194", "\194\065", "\224\128\128",
    "\224\159\191", "\237\160\128", "\237\191\191", "\240\128\128\128",
    "\240\143\191\191", "\244\144\128\128", "\245\128\128\128", "\255",
    "\226\130\065", "\240\159\152\065", "\226\130", "\240\159\152",
}

function M.theFusedScanFindsTheSameBadByteAtEveryVectorOffset()
    -- The checks above are all short enough to take the byte-at-a-time tail.
    -- These push the same sequences past whole vectors, so the lookup4
    -- validator is what finds them and its lane is what names the byte. The
    -- padding is ASCII inside a string, and a trailing quote is omitted on
    -- purpose: the UTF-8 error comes first in byte order either way.
    local checked = 0
    for _, bad in ipairs(BAD_UTF8) do
        for pad = 0, 72 do
            local text = '"' .. string.rep("a", pad) .. bad .. '"'
            local code, position = referenceScan(text)
            assert(code == INVALID_UTF8, string.format("the reference missed %s at pad %d", show(text), pad))
            local _, message = decodedBy(fused, text)
            assert(message ~= nil, string.format("%s decoded but holds bad UTF-8", show(text)))
            local reported = tonumber(message:match("at byte (%d+)"))
            assert(
                reported == position,
                string.format("%s raises at byte %s but the reference says %d", show(text), tostring(reported), position)
            )
            checked = checked + 1
        end
    end
    assert(checked > 1000, "only " .. checked .. " offsets were checked")
end

function M.wellFormedUnicodeSurvivesEveryVectorOffset()
    -- The same sweep for text that is valid, so a validator that is merely
    -- eager cannot pass the check above.
    local scalars = {"\194\128", "\223\191", "\224\160\128", "\239\191\191",
        "\240\144\128\128", "\244\143\191\191", "\226\130\172"}
    for _, scalar in ipairs(scalars) do
        for pad = 0, 72 do
            local text = '"' .. string.rep("a", pad) .. scalar .. string.rep("b", 3) .. '"'
            local mine, myError = decodedBy(fused, text)
            local theirs = decodedBy(lunajson, text)
            assert(myError == nil, string.format("%s was refused: %s", show(text), tostring(myError)))
            assert(mine == theirs, string.format("%s decoded differently from lunajson", show(text)))
        end
    end
end

function M.theScalarReferenceAcceptsEveryWellFormedCorpusDocument()
    for _, text in ipairs(corpus()) do
        local code, position = referenceScan(text)
        assert(code == OK, string.format("the reference rejected the well-formed %s at byte %d", show(text), position))
    end
end

function M.decodingIsUnchangedByTheSourceLength()
    -- One document at every offset a vector may start on, so the whole-vector
    -- path and the byte-at-a-time tail both cover every byte of it.
    for pad = 0, 65 do
        local text = string.rep(" ", pad) .. '{"a":[1,"b\\n",null,true],"c":{"d":-2.5}}'
        local mine, myError = decodedBy(fused, text)
        local theirs = decodedBy(lunajson, text)
        assert(myError == nil, string.format("padding by %d broke the decoder: %s", pad, tostring(myError)))
        assert(mine == theirs, string.format("padding by %d changed the value", pad))
    end
end

-- Sweep sparse Unicode transitions and short tails across vector boundaries.
-- A later malformed sequence must never displace the first error in the input.
function M.scanPreservesSparseUnicodeTransitionsAndFirstErrors()
    local euro, smile = "\226\130\172", "\240\159\152\128"
    for pad = 0, 260 do
        for _, gap in ipairs({0, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 65, 127, 128, 129}) do
            local text = '"' .. string.rep("a", pad) .. euro .. string.rep("b", gap) .. smile .. string.rep("c", pad % 67) .. '"'
            local mine, message = decodedBy(fused, text)
            local theirs, other = decodedBy(lunajson, text)
            assert(message == nil and other == nil, "mixed Unicode refused at " .. pad .. ":" .. gap .. ": " .. tostring(message))
            assert(mine == theirs, "mixed Unicode changed at " .. pad .. ":" .. gap)
        end
        for _, bad in ipairs(BAD_UTF8) do
            for _, suffix in ipairs({"", string.rep("z", 65)}) do
                local text = '"' .. string.rep("a", pad) .. bad .. suffix .. '"'
                local code, position = referenceScan(text)
                assert(code == INVALID_UTF8, "reference missed malformed UTF-8")
                local _, message = decodedBy(fused, text)
                local reported = message and tonumber(message:match("at byte (%d+)"))
                assert(reported == position, "malformed UTF-8 at " .. pad .. ": " .. tostring(reported) .. " vs " .. position)
            end
        end
        -- A control error before later malformed Unicode stays first.
        local text = '"' .. string.rep("a", pad) .. "\001" .. string.rep("b", 65) .. "\255\""
        local code, position = referenceScan(text)
        assert(code == INVALID_CONTROL)
        local _, message = decodedBy(fused, text)
        assert(message and tonumber(message:match("at byte (%d+)")) == position, "later Unicode displaced earlier control error")
    end
end

-- Exercise every byte class on both sides of the ASCII/Unicode transition,
-- with enough following bytes to cover full vectors as well as short tails.
function M.everyByteClassPreservesValuesAndFirstErrorsAcrossTransitions()
    for _, prefix in ipairs({"", "\226\130\172"}) do
        for pad = 0, 80 do
            for byte = 0, 255 do
                for _, tail in ipairs({"", string.rep("z", 17)}) do
                    local text = '"' .. prefix .. string.rep("a", pad) .. string.char(byte) .. tail .. '"'
                    local code, position = referenceScan(text)
                    local mine, message = decodedBy(fused, text)
                    local theirs, other = decodedBy(lunajson, text)
                    assert((message == nil) == (other == nil), "byte-class acceptance at " .. pad .. ":" .. byte)
                    if code ~= OK then
                        local reported = message and tonumber(message:match("at byte (%d+)"))
                        assert(reported == position, "byte-class error at " .. pad .. ":" .. byte .. ": " .. tostring(reported) .. " vs " .. position)
                    elseif message == nil then
                        assert(mine == theirs, "byte-class value at " .. pad .. ":" .. byte)
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    end
end

return M

forks,samples=(3,7) if stage=='pilot' else (25,25)

guarded_but_contaminated.retention_pass_annotation: Historical raw summary.retention_pass checks performance ratio intervals only. It does not assert control quality, environmental eligibility, or overall retention. The historical summary is preserved unchanged.

protocol.retention_rule: ASCII throughput CI lower >1/.99; both Unicode CI lower >1/1.01; every control CV <=5 percent; correctness and actual native execution proofs pass.
protocol.environment_rule: Before each process require5seconds without other active compiler/test activity; the quiet interval carries across our own monitored measurement processes, which are excluded from interference; sample every0.2seconds throughout. A process is eligible only if no interference is observed throughout and it exits successfully. Eligibility uses process activity only, never duration or throughput. All attempts, including ineligible ones, retained. Collect exactly25eligible independent processes per payload, with rotating payload order. Max150attempts and900seconds from the first measurement launch, with a separate1800second initial idle-wait allowance; fail rather than relax limits. No further retry based on numerical results.
protocol.qualification_change: Three full runs were invalidated by objective external activity. The first short-window launch was interrupted after waiting with zero measurement attempts; only its idle-wait allowance is extended here, before any performance data exists. A second wait-only launch also collected zero attempts; before sampling, the implementation was corrected to carry the continuous external-quiet interval across our own processes rather than unnecessarily resetting it for every process. A third wait-only launch also collected zero attempts; deadline checks were corrected before sampling to enforce the measurement deadline before each launch and during process polling, not only while waiting for quiet. Short clean windows replace requiring uninterrupted silence for the entire125-second batch. Frozen artifacts, per-process measurement, numerical thresholds and analysis are unchanged. No earlier observations are reclassified or reused.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Finalize #63 evidence after collection completes; never run measurements.

Run only when authorized by the coordinating agent. All checks precede writes.
Existing evidence is retained, and a second invocation refuses to overwrite it.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import collections
import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import math
import statistics

ROOT = Path('/private/tmp/nupp-mask-any-scan')
RUN = Path('/private/tmp/nupp-63-events-carry-window-final-formal')
EVIDENCE = ROOT / 'bench/fused-json/results/arm64-macos-mask-any-events.json'
MARKDOWN = EVIDENCE.with_suffix('.md')
HARNESS = ROOT / 'bench/fused-json/tests/bench.lua'
HARNESS_SHA = '4f24d4232bb1b63960ec23ef3826fa001d682a7119f5278441633ccf13015524'
BASE = Path('/private/tmp/nupp-63-baseline')
CANDIDATE = Path('/private/tmp/nupp-63-events-carry-candidate')
PAYLOADS = ('ascii', 'unicode', 'sparseUnicode')
WAIT_NAMES = ('window-formal', 'window-final-wait-only', 'window-deadline-wait-only')
SCOPE = (
    'No disqualifying activity observed at nominal 0.2-second process samples. '
    'The detector flags cargo, rustc, clang, clang++, cc1, cc, gcc, ninja, make '
    'and cmake at any reported CPU usage, and lua/luajit or names starting '
    'with nupp above 5% ps CPU, excluding the measurement process group. '
    'Other executable names and jobs occurring entirely between samples are '
    'outside this detection claim; this is not proof of an idle machine.'
)


def require(condition, message):
    if not condition:
        raise RuntimeError(message)


def digest(data):
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


def read_json(path):
    return json.loads(path.read_text())


def file_record(path):
    raw = path.read_bytes()
    return {'path': str(path), 'bytes': len(raw), 'sha256': digest(raw),
            'text': raw.decode('utf-8')}


def observations(path):
    record = file_record(path)
    rows = [json.loads(line) for line in record['text'].splitlines() if line]
    allowed = {'utc', 'phase', 'attempt', 'interference'}
    require(bool(rows), 'Missing environment observations: ' + str(path))
    require(all(set(row) == allowed for row in rows),
            'Unexpected environment schema; review before publishing')
    return record, rows


def zero_attempt_record(name):
    directory = Path('/private/tmp/nupp-63-events-carry-' + name)
    require(directory.is_dir(), 'Missing preserved wait-only directory ' + str(directory))
    require(not list(directory.glob('attempt-*')), 'Wait-only directory contains attempts')
    require(not list(directory.glob('*-??.json')), 'Wait-only directory contains selected results')
    _, rows = observations(directory / 'environment.jsonl')
    require(all(row['attempt'] == 0 and row['phase'] == 'waiting' for row in rows),
            'A supposedly wait-only run sampled a measurement')
    require(not (directory / 'environment-qualified.json').exists(),
            'A wait-only run claims completion')
    files = {p.name: file_record(p) for p in sorted(directory.iterdir()) if p.is_file()}
    return {'directory': str(directory), 'measurement_started': False,
            'attempts': 0, 'status': 'interrupted while waiting; no performance samples',
            'protocol': read_json(directory / 'protocol.json'), 'files': files,
            'environment_file': 'environment.jsonl',
            'execution_log': file_record(Path(str(directory) + '-run.log'))}


def analyze(forks):
    rows = []
    for payload in PAYLOADS:
        data = [fork['result']['payloads'][0] for fork in forks if fork['payload'] == payload]
        require(len(data) == 25, 'Expected 25 eligible processes per payload')
        first = data[0]
        require(all(d['digest'] == first['digest'] and d['bytes'] == first['bytes'] for d in data),
                'Payload identity differs between processes')
        paired = [statistics.median(math.log(a / b) for a, b in
                  zip(d['fused']['samples'], d['baseline']['samples'])) for d in data]
        center = statistics.mean(paired)
        delta = 2.0638985616 * statistics.stdev(paired) / math.sqrt(25)
        low, high = math.exp(center - delta), math.exp(center + delta)
        verdict = ('improved' if low > 1 / .99 else 'regressed' if high < 1 / 1.01 else
                   'unchanged' if low >= 1 / 1.01 and high <= 1 / .99 else 'inconclusive')
        control = [d['lunajson']['median'] for d in data]
        rows.append({'payload': payload, 'bytes': first['bytes'], 'digest': first['digest'],
                     'forks': 25, 'candidate_MBps': statistics.median(d['fused']['median'] for d in data),
                     'baseline_MBps': statistics.median(d['baseline']['median'] for d in data),
                     'throughput_ratio': math.exp(center), 'ratio_CI95': [low, high],
                     'duration_change_percent': 100 * (1 / math.exp(center) - 1),
                     'duration_basis': 'process CPU time from os.clock(), not wall-clock latency',
                     'verdict': verdict, 'control_MBps': statistics.median(control),
                     'control_min_max': [min(control), max(control)],
                     'control_cv_percent': 100 * statistics.stdev(control) / statistics.mean(control),
                     'fork_paired_log_ratios': paired})
    return {'payloads': rows,
            'performance_gates_pass': rows[0]['ratio_CI95'][0] > 1 / .99 and
            all(row['ratio_CI95'][0] > 1 / 1.01 for row in rows[1:]),
            'control_quality_pass': all(row['control_cv_percent'] <= 5 for row in rows)}


def main():
    original_json = EVIDENCE.read_bytes()
    original_md = MARKDOWN.read_bytes()
    evidence = json.loads(original_json)
    candidate = evidence['candidates']['event_with_carry']
    require('qualified_formal' not in candidate['runs'], 'Final evidence already exists; refusing overwrite')
    completion = read_json(RUN / 'environment-qualified.json')
    require(completion.get('qualified') is True and completion.get('eligible_processes') == 75,
            'Collector has not completed 75 qualified processes')
    protocol = read_json(RUN / 'protocol.json')
    expected = {'forks_per_payload': 25, 'samples_per_fork': 25, 'warmups': 3,
                'native_batch_bytes': 67108864, 'control_batch_bytes': 2097152,
                'primary': 'ascii', 'ceilings': ['unicode', 'sparseUnicode'], 'margin_percent': 1}
    require(all(protocol.get(k) == v for k, v in expected.items()), 'Frozen numerical protocol changed')
    require(protocol['hashes'].get(str(HARNESS)) == HARNESS_SHA,
            'Native-execution proof harness is not the reviewed frozen version')
    require(all(digest(Path(path).read_bytes()) == sha for path, sha in protocol['hashes'].items()),
            'A frozen measured artifact has changed')
    environment, samples = observations(RUN / 'environment.jsonl')
    measured = collections.defaultdict(list)
    for row in samples:
        if row['phase'] == 'measurement':
            measured[row['attempt']].append(row)
    attempts, forks = [], []
    selected = set()
    launch_times = []
    quiet_checks = []
    directories = sorted(p for p in RUN.glob('attempt-*') if p.is_dir())
    require(len(directories) == completion['attempts'] and 75 <= len(directories) <= 150,
            'Attempt inventory does not match completion or budget')
    for number, directory in enumerate(directories, 1):
        eligibility = read_json(directory / 'eligibility.json')
        require(eligibility['attempt'] == number and eligibility['directory'] == directory.name,
                'Attempt numbering or identity mismatch')
        require(eligibility['exit_code'] == 0, 'A failed semantic/native proof attempt cannot be retried')
        rows = measured[number]
        require(bool(rows), 'Attempt has no environment samples')
        interference = any(row['interference'] for row in rows)
        require(eligibility['interference'] == interference and eligibility['eligible'] == (not interference),
                'Eligibility disagrees with raw process observations')
        result = read_json(directory / 'result.json')
        log = (directory / 'output.log').read_text()
        require(result['samples'] == 25 and len(result['payloads']) == 1, 'Invalid result sample count')
        payload = result['payloads'][0]
        require(payload['payload'] == eligibility['payload'] and payload['payload'] in PAYLOADS,
                'Attempt payload identity mismatch')
        for implementation in ('fused', 'baseline', 'lunajson'):
            values = payload[implementation]['samples']
            require(len(values) == 25 and all(math.isfinite(v) and v > 0 for v in values),
                    'Invalid paired samples or control samples')
        for key, base in (('artifact', CANDIDATE), ('baselineArtifact', BASE)):
            require(Path(result[key]).resolve() == (base / 'nupp/codec/json/internal/decoder/fusedbench.lua').resolve(),
                    'Native artifact route differs from the frozen comparison')
        for key, base in (('object', CANDIDATE), ('baselineObject', BASE)):
            require(Path(result[key]).resolve() == (base / 'lib/libfused_json_aot.dylib').resolve(),
                    'Observed native builder does not come from the expected object')
        require('compiled decoder proof' in log and 'baseline compiled decoder:' in log,
                'Missing successful native-proof execution log')
        files = {p.name: file_record(p) for p in sorted(directory.iterdir()) if p.is_file()}
        attempts.append({'name': directory.name, 'eligibility': eligibility, 'result': result,
                         'log': log, 'files': files})
        if eligibility['eligible']:
            launch = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(eligibility['started_utc'])
            quiet_start = None
            latest_observation = None
            for observation in samples:
                observed_at = datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(observation['utc'])
                if observed_at > launch:
                    break
                latest_observation = observed_at
                if observation['interference']:
                    quiet_start = None
                elif quiet_start is None:
                    quiet_start = observed_at
            require(quiet_start is not None and latest_observation is not None,
                    'Eligible launch has no preceding sampled quiet interval')
            quiet_seconds = (launch - quiet_start).total_seconds()
            require(quiet_seconds >= 5,
                    'Eligible launch lacks the required five-second sampled quiet interval')
            quiet_checks.append({'attempt': number, 'launch_utc': eligibility['started_utc'],
                                 'quiet_since_utc': quiet_start.isoformat(),
                                 'sampled_quiet_seconds': quiet_seconds,
                                 'last_prelaunch_observation_utc': latest_observation.isoformat()})
            key = (eligibility['payload'], eligibility['fork'])
            require(key not in selected and 1 <= key[1] <= 25, 'Duplicate/out-of-range eligible fork')
            selected.add(key)
            name = '%s-%02d' % key
            require((RUN / (name + '.json')).read_bytes() == (directory / 'result.json').read_bytes(),
                    'Selected result is not its original eligible attempt')
            require((RUN / (name + '.log')).read_text() == log, 'Selected log differs from attempt log')
            forks.append({'name': name, 'payload': key[0], 'attempt': number, 'result': result, 'log': log})
        launch_times.append(datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(eligibility['started_utc']))
    require(selected == {(p, n) for p in PAYLOADS for n in range(1, 26)}, 'Missing eligible forks')
    require(len(forks) == 75, 'Expected exactly 75 eligible processes')
    first_launch = min(launch_times)
    last_measurement = max(datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(row['utc'])
                           for row in samples if row['phase'] == 'measurement')
    observed_window_seconds = (last_measurement - first_launch).total_seconds()
    require(0 <= observed_window_seconds <= 900,
            'Last observed measurement exceeds the frozen 900-second window')
    completed_at = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(
        (RUN / 'environment-qualified.json').stat().st_mtime, datetime.timezone.utc)
    window = {'first_launch_utc': first_launch.isoformat(),
              'last_measurement_observation_utc': last_measurement.isoformat(),
              'observed_measurement_window_wall_seconds': observed_window_seconds,
              'within_900_second_observed_window': True,
              'completion_file_mtime_utc': completed_at.isoformat(),
              'launch_to_completion_file_wall_seconds': (completed_at - first_launch).total_seconds(),
              'scope': 'UTC observation span includes intervening waits and rejected attempts. '
                       'Completion time is preserved filesystem metadata, not a timed decode sample.'}
    summary = analyze(forks)
    correctness = ('9 tests, 9 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed' in candidate['tests.log'] and
                   all('9 compiled decoder differential tests passed' in candidate[k]
                       for k in ('differentials.log', 'baseline-differentials.log')) and
                   'fixpoint ok:' in candidate['fixpoint.log'] and
                   candidate['integrated_compiler_check']['identical_to_frozen_measured_c'] is True and
                   '9 compiled decoder differential tests passed' in
                   candidate['integrated_compiler_check']['compiled_differentials'])
    gates = {'performance': summary['performance_gates_pass'], 'control_cv': summary['control_quality_pass'],
             'environment': True, 'native_execution_proofs': True, 'correctness': correctness}
    print(json.dumps({'summary': summary, 'gates': gates}, indent=2), flush=True)
    require(all(gates.values()), 'A frozen retention gate failed; no evidence files were modified')
    waits = [zero_attempt_record(name) for name in WAIT_NAMES]
    record = {'protocol': protocol, 'protocol_file': file_record(RUN / 'protocol.json'),
              'summary': summary, 'forks': forks, 'attempts': attempts,
              'execution_log': Path(str(RUN) + '-run.log').read_text(),
              'environment': {'completion': completion, 'raw_observations': environment,
                              'detection_scope': SCOPE, 'qualified': True,
                              'measurement_window': window, 'eligible_launch_quiet_checks': quiet_checks},
              'gates': gates, 'overall_retention_pass': True,
              'native_execution_proof': {'harness_sha256': HARNESS_SHA,
                  'method': 'Each successful process runs reviewed proveCompiled call hooks for both exports, '
                            'asserts registered native C execution, and asserts distinct native builders. '
                            'Observed artifact/object routes are checked against the frozen paths.'},
              'timing_basis': 'process CPU time from os.clock(); no wall-clock latency claim',
              'environment_exclusions': len(attempts) - 75,
              'wait_only_runs': waits, 'finalizer': file_record(Path(__file__))}
    historical = {
        name: digest(json.dumps(run['summary'], sort_keys=True).encode())
        for name, run in candidate['runs'].items() if 'summary' in run}
    for old_candidate in evidence['candidates'].values():
        for name, run in old_candidate['runs'].items():
            if 'retention_pass' in run.get('summary', {}):
                run['retention_pass_annotation'] = (
                    'Historical raw summary.retention_pass checks performance ratio intervals only. '
                    'It does not assert control quality, environmental eligibility, or overall retention. '
                    'The historical summary is preserved unchanged.')
    candidate['runs']['qualified_formal'] = record
    candidate['retained'] = True
    candidate['overall_retention_pass'] = True
    candidate['qualification'] = ('Retained by qualified_formal only: all frozen performance, control-CV, '
                                  'sampled-environment, native-execution and correctness gates pass. '
                                  'Earlier contaminated measurements remain disqualified.')
    evidence['overall_retention_pass'] = True
    evidence['authoritative_retention_run'] = 'candidates.event_with_carry.runs.qualified_formal'
    evidence['historical_retention_summary_semantics'] = (
        'All pre-final summary.retention_pass fields are numerical performance gates only; '
        'raw historical summaries have not been changed.')
    require(all(digest(json.dumps(candidate['runs'][k]['summary'], sort_keys=True).encode()) == value
                for k, value in historical.items()), 'Historical summaries changed')
    md = original_md.decode('utf-8')
    old = ('Any external compiler activity invalidates that entire run regardless of its\n'
           'performance result.')
    require(old in md, 'Expected historical environment paragraph changed; review MD update')
    md = md.replace(old, 'Under that earlier full-run protocol, observed disqualifying activity invalidated\n'
                    'the entire run regardless of its performance result.', 1)
    md = md.replace('without accepting overlap within them.',
                    'while excluding processes with observed disqualifying activity.')
    lines = ['## Qualified final result', '',
             'The event-and-carry candidate passes every frozen retention gate. These are',
             '**process-CPU-time throughput** measurements using `os.clock()`, not wall-clock',
             'latency measurements. Ratios are candidate/baseline; intervals are 95% Student',
             't intervals over 25 independent process-level median paired log ratios.', '',
             '| Payload | Throughput ratio (95% interval) | CPU-duration change | Control CV |',
             '| --- | --- | --- | --- |']
    labels = {'ascii': 'ASCII', 'unicode': 'Dense Unicode', 'sparseUnicode': 'Sparse Unicode'}

                      row['duration_change_percent'], row['control_cv_percent']))

              (len(attempts), len(attempts) - 75),
              'solely by sampled process activity. Every attempt, eligibility decision, output log,',
              'raw environment observation, frozen protocol/script, and all three earlier',
              'zero-attempt waits remain in the complete record. No numerical gates changed.', '',
              'The observed measurement window spans %.2f wall seconds from the first launch' %
              observed_window_seconds,
              'through the last measurement observation, including waits and rejected attempts;',
              'all 75 eligible launches have at least five seconds of preceding sampled quiet.', '',
              SCOPE, '',
              'Historical `retention_pass` fields describe performance intervals only; their raw',

event_with_carry.jsonfuseddifferentialtest.lua:
-- The AOT fused JSON decoder and the Lunajson provider are two independent
-- readings of the same grammar: one scans with vectors and walks a structural
-- tape, the other is a third-party byte-at-a-time parser Nupp did not write.
-- Where they agree on a corpus they agree because both read JSON, not because
-- one was derived from the other.
--
-- The scan itself is checked a second way, against `referenceScan` below. That
-- is this file's independent scalar reference in the sense
-- `bench/simd-json/src/simd_json/indexer_reference.nupp` is the vector
-- indexer's: it shares no mask, no lane and no tape with the decoder, and it
-- states the same contract -- the first error in byte order, and the one-based
-- position of the byte that raised it.
--
-- Nothing here builds anything. With no linked artifact the `@aot` body runs
-- as ordinary Nupp, which is the same source and the same answers; what it
-- does not exercise is the emitted C, which the `aot` group covers. Every
-- literal below is ASCII, so a byte sequence under test is written as an
-- escape and never as itself.

local fused = require("nupp.codec.json.aot")
local lunajson = require("nupp.runtime.provider.lunajson")

local M = {}

local NULL = setmetatable({}, {__tostring = function() return "null" end})

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The shared corpus
----------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Documents both decoders must accept and agree on.
local WELL_FORMED = {
    -- Scalars and the whitespace around them.
    "0", "-0", "1", "-1", "123456789", "  42  ", "\t\r\n7\n", "true", "false", "null",
    '""', '"a"', '"hello world"',

    -- Numbers at and around the edges of binary64.
    "1e308", "-1e308", "1.7976931348623157e308", "-1.7976931348623157e308",
    "5e-324", "-5e-324", "2.2250738585072014e-308", "1e-323",
    "9007199254740991", "9007199254740992", "-9007199254740991",
    "0.1", "0.2", "0.30000000000000004", "1e-7", "1E+7", "1e0", "-0.0",
    "123456789012345678901234567890", "0.000000000000000000001",
    "1.000000000000000000000000000000001", "3.141592653589793",

    -- Containers, nesting and mixed shapes.
    "[]", "{}", "[[]]", "[{}]", '{"a":{}}', "[1,2,3]", "[1,[2,[3,[4]]]]",
    '{"a":1,"b":2,"c":3}', '{"a":[1,2],"b":{"c":[3]}}',
    '[null,true,false,0,"",[],{}]',
    '{"":1}', '{"a":null,"b":null}',
    "[ 1 , 2 , 3 ]", '{ "a" : 1 }',
    '{"a":[{"b":[{"c":[{"d":1}]}]}]}',

    -- Escapes, including every simple one and the pair a supplementary
    -- codepoint needs. These are long strings, so a backslash here is the
    -- backslash the decoder sees.
    [["\""]], [["\\"]], [["\/"]], [["\b"]], [["\f"]], [["\n"]], [["\r"]], [["\t"]],
    [["\u0041"]], [["\u00e9"]], [["\u0020"]], [["\u0001"]], [["\u001f"]],
    [["\u00ff"]], [["\u0800"]], [["\uffff"]], [["\ud83d\ude00"]], [["\udbff\udfff"]],
    [["a\\b"]], [["a\\\\b"]], [["\\\""]], [["\\\\\""]], [["a\nb\tc"]],
    [["\u0041\u0042\u0043"]],
    [[{"k\"ey":"v\\alue"}]],
    [[{"\u0041":"\u00e9"}]],

    -- Literal UTF-8 of every scalar length, written as byte escapes.
    '"\195\169"', '"\226\130\172"', '"\240\159\152\128"',
    '"\194\128"', '"\223\191"', '"\224\160\128"', '"\239\191\191"',
    '"\240\144\128\128"', '"\244\143\191\191"',
    '{"\226\130\172":"\240\159\152\128"}',
}

-- Inputs neither decoder may accept.
local MALFORMED = {
    "", "   ", "\n",
    "tru", "fals", "nul", "trues", "True", "NULL",
    "+1", "01", "-", "1.", ".1", "1e", "1e+", "--1", "1.2.3", "Infinity", "NaN",
    "[", "]", "{", "}", "[1", '{"a"', '{"a":', '{"a":1', "[1,", "[1,]", "{,}", "[,]",
    '{"a":1,}', '{"a" 1}', "{a:1}", "{'a':1}", "[1 2]", '{"a":1"b":2}',
    '"unterminated', '"a\\"', '"\\"', '"\\q"', '"\\u"', '"\\u12"', '"\\uZZZZ"',
    [["\ud800"]], [["\udc00"]], [["\ud800\ud800"]], [["\ud800x"]],
    "[1,2,3]extra", "{} {}", "1 2", "null null",
    -- Control bytes are never literal inside a string.
    '"\001"', '"\009"', '"\010"', '"\031"',
    -- A backslash outside a string is not a token.
    "[\\]", "\\", '{"a":\\}',
    -- Malformed UTF-8 of every failing shape.
    '"\128"', '"\191"', '"\192\128"', '"\193\191"', '"\194"', '"\224\128\128"',
    '"\224\159\191"', '"\237\160\128"', '"\240\128\128\128"', '"\244\144\128\128"',
    '"\245\128\128\128"', '"\255"', '"\226\130"', '"\240\159\152"',
    '\226\130\172', '"a\128b"',
}

-- Deep containers, built rather than written out.
local function nested(open, close, depth)
    return string.rep(open, depth) .. "1" .. string.rep(close, depth)
end

local function wideArray(count)
    local parts = {}
    for i = 1, count do
        parts[i] = tostring(i)
    end

    return "[" .. table.concat(parts, ",") .. "]"
end

local function wideObject(count)
    local parts = {}
    for i = 1, count do
        parts[i] = string.format('"k%d":%d', i, i)
    end

    return "{" .. table.concat(parts, ",") .. "}"
end

local function corpus()
    local all = {}
    for _, text in ipairs(WELL_FORMED) do
        all[#all + 1] = text
    end
    for depth = 1, 24 do
        all[#all + 1] = nested("[", "]", depth)
    end
    for _, count in ipairs({1, 2, 3, 15, 16, 17, 31, 32, 33, 63, 64, 65, 200}) do
        all[#all + 1] = wideArray(count)
        all[#all + 1] = wideObject(count)
    end
    -- Strings that straddle every plausible vector and block boundary, plain
    -- and escaped, so the whole-vector path and the byte-at-a-time tail both
    -- cover every shape at least once.
    for length = 0, 80 do
        all[#all + 1] = '"' .. string.rep("a", length) .. '"'
        all[#all + 1] = '["' .. string.rep("a", length) .. '","b"]'
        all[#all + 1] = '"' .. string.rep("\\n", length) .. '"'
        all[#all + 1] = '"' .. string.rep("a", length) .. '\\u00e9"'
        all[#all + 1] = '{"' .. string.rep("k", length) .. '":1}'
        all[#all + 1] = string.rep(" ", length) .. "[1]"
        all[#all + 1] = '"' .. string.rep("\226\130\172", length) .. '"'
    end
    -- Backslash runs of every parity across a vector boundary.
    for slashes = 1, 40 do
        all[#all + 1] = '"' .. string.rep("\\", slashes * 2) .. '"'
        all[#all + 1] = '"' .. string.rep("a", slashes) .. '\\\\"'
    end

    return all
end

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The independent scalar reference for the structural scan
----------------------------------------------------------------------------

local OK, INVALID_UTF8, INVALID_CONTROL, INVALID_BACKSLASH = 0, 2, 3, 4

-- Reads `source` one byte after another and keeps what a JSON structural scan
-- needs: whether it is inside a string, the parity of the backslash run before
-- the current byte, and for UTF-8 how many continuation bytes the last lead
-- still owes and what range the first of them must fall in.
--
-- Answers the first scan error in byte order as a code and the one-based
-- position of the byte that raised it, or `OK, 0`. A UTF-8 scalar the end of
-- the input cut off is raised one past the last byte. It says nothing about
-- the grammar above the bytes; that is what the decoders are compared on.
local function referenceScan(source)
    local inString, slashRun = false, 0
    local owed, constraint, lastNonAscii = 0, 0, -1

    for offset = 0, #source - 1 do
        local byte = source:byte(offset + 1)
        if owed > 0 then
            local continuation = byte >= 128 and byte <= 191
            local outside = constraint == 1 and byte < 160
                or constraint == 2 and byte > 159
                or constraint == 3 and byte < 144
                or constraint == 4 and byte > 143
            if not continuation or outside then
                return INVALID_UTF8, offset + 1
            end
            owed, constraint, lastNonAscii, slashRun = owed - 1, 0, offset, 0
        elseif byte >= 128 then
            if byte < 194 or byte > 244 then
                return INVALID_UTF8, offset + 1
            elseif byte <= 223 then
                owed = 1
            elseif byte <= 239 then
                owed = 2
                if byte == 224 then
                    constraint = 1
                elseif byte == 237 then
                    constraint = 2
                end
            else
                owed = 3
                if byte == 240 then
                    constraint = 3
                elseif byte == 244 then
                    constraint = 4
                end
            end
            lastNonAscii, slashRun = offset, 0
        elseif byte == 92 then
            if not inString then
                return INVALID_BACKSLASH, offset + 1
            end
            slashRun = slashRun + 1
        else
            local escaped = slashRun % 2 == 1
            slashRun = 0
            if byte == 34 and not escaped then
                inString = not inString
            elseif byte < 32 then
                if inString or not (byte == 9 or byte == 10 or byte == 13) then
                    return INVALID_CONTROL, offset + 1
                end
            end
        end
    end

    if owed > 0 then
        return INVALID_UTF8, lastNonAscii + 2
    end

    return OK, 0
end

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Comparison
----------------------------------------------------------------------------

local function render(value, seen)
    local kind = type(value)
    if value == NULL then
        return "null"
    elseif kind ~= "table" then
        if kind == "number" then
            return string.format("%.17g", value)
        end

        return kind .. ":" .. tostring(value)
    end
    seen = seen or {}
    assert(not seen[value], "the decoded value is cyclic")
    seen[value] = true
    local keys = {}
    for key in pairs(value) do
        keys[#keys + 1] = key
    end
    local array = true
    for index = 1, #keys do
        if value[index] == nil then
            array = false
            break
        end
    end
    local parts = {}
    if array then
        for index = 1, #keys do
            parts[index] = render(value[index], seen)
        end
        seen[value] = nil

        return "[" .. table.concat(parts, ",") .. "]"
    end
    table.sort(keys, function(left, right) return tostring(left) < tostring(right) end)
    for index, key in ipairs(keys) do
        parts[index] = string.format("%q", tostring(key)) .. ":" .. render(value[key], seen)
    end
    seen[value] = nil

    return "{" .. table.concat(parts, ",") .. "}"
end

local function decodedBy(provider, text)
    local ok, value = pcall(provider.decode, text, NULL)
    if not ok then
        return nil, tostring(value)
    end

    return render(value), nil
end

local function show(text)
    return (text:gsub("[^\032-\126]", function(c)
        return string.format("<%d>", c:byte())
    end)):sub(1, 60)
end

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The checks
----------------------------------------------------------------------------

function M.theFusedDecoderDecodesEveryCorpusDocumentAsLunajsonDoes()
    local checked = 0
    for _, text in ipairs(corpus()) do
        local mine, myError = decodedBy(fused, text)
        local theirs, theirError = decodedBy(lunajson, text)
        assert(
            myError == nil and theirError == nil,
            string.format(
                "%s should be well formed for both: fused=%s lunajson=%s",
                show(text),
                tostring(myError),
                tostring(theirError)
            )
        )
        assert(mine == theirs, string.format("%s decodes to %s but lunajson says %s", show(text), mine, theirs))
        checked = checked + 1
    end
    assert(checked > 700, "the corpus shrank to " .. checked .. " documents")
end

function M.theFusedDecoderRejectsEveryDocumentLunajsonRejects()
    for _, text in ipairs(MALFORMED) do
        local mine, myError = decodedBy(fused, text)
        local theirs, theirError = decodedBy(lunajson, text)
        assert(myError ~= nil, string.format("%s decoded to %s but is malformed", show(text), tostring(mine)))
        assert(
            theirError ~= nil,
            string.format("lunajson accepted the malformed %s as %s", show(text), tostring(theirs))
        )
    end
end

function M.theFusedScanReportsTheSameFirstErrorAsTheScalarReference()
    local checked = 0
    for _, text in ipairs(MALFORMED) do
        local code, position = referenceScan(text)
        if code ~= OK then
            local _, message = decodedBy(fused, text)
            assert(message ~= nil, string.format("%s decoded, but the reference raises %d at %d", show(text), code, position))
            local reported = tonumber(message:match("at byte (%d+)"))
            assert(reported ~= nil, string.format("%s reported %q, which names no byte", show(text), message))
            assert(
                reported == position,
                string.format("%s raises at byte %d but the reference says %d", show(text), reported, position)
            )
            checked = checked + 1
        end
    end
    assert(checked > 20, "the reference agreed on only " .. checked .. " inputs")
end

-- Malformed byte sequences on their own, to be placed at a chosen offset.
local BAD_UTF8 = {
    "\128", "\191", "\192\128", "\193\191", "\194", "\194\065", "\224\128\128",
    "\224\159\191", "\237\160\128", "\237\191\191", "\240\128\128\128",
    "\240\143\191\191", "\244\144\128\128", "\245\128\128\128", "\255",
    "\226\130\065", "\240\159\152\065", "\226\130", "\240\159\152",
}

function M.theFusedScanFindsTheSameBadByteAtEveryVectorOffset()
    -- The checks above are all short enough to take the byte-at-a-time tail.
    -- These push the same sequences past whole vectors, so the lookup4
    -- validator is what finds them and its lane is what names the byte. The
    -- padding is ASCII inside a string, and a trailing quote is omitted on
    -- purpose: the UTF-8 error comes first in byte order either way.
    local checked = 0
    for _, bad in ipairs(BAD_UTF8) do
        for pad = 0, 72 do
            local text = '"' .. string.rep("a", pad) .. bad .. '"'
            local code, position = referenceScan(text)
            assert(code == INVALID_UTF8, string.format("the reference missed %s at pad %d", show(text), pad))
            local _, message = decodedBy(fused, text)
            assert(message ~= nil, string.format("%s decoded but holds bad UTF-8", show(text)))
            local reported = tonumber(message:match("at byte (%d+)"))
            assert(
                reported == position,
                string.format("%s raises at byte %s but the reference says %d", show(text), tostring(reported), position)
            )
            checked = checked + 1
        end
    end
    assert(checked > 1000, "only " .. checked .. " offsets were checked")
end

function M.wellFormedUnicodeSurvivesEveryVectorOffset()
    -- The same sweep for text that is valid, so a validator that is merely
    -- eager cannot pass the check above.
    local scalars = {"\194\128", "\223\191", "\224\160\128", "\239\191\191",
        "\240\144\128\128", "\244\143\191\191", "\226\130\172"}
    for _, scalar in ipairs(scalars) do
        for pad = 0, 72 do
            local text = '"' .. string.rep("a", pad) .. scalar .. string.rep("b", 3) .. '"'
            local mine, myError = decodedBy(fused, text)
            local theirs = decodedBy(lunajson, text)
            assert(myError == nil, string.format("%s was refused: %s", show(text), tostring(myError)))
            assert(mine == theirs, string.format("%s decoded differently from lunajson", show(text)))
        end
    end
end

function M.theScalarReferenceAcceptsEveryWellFormedCorpusDocument()
    for _, text in ipairs(corpus()) do
        local code, position = referenceScan(text)
        assert(code == OK, string.format("the reference rejected the well-formed %s at byte %d", show(text), position))
    end
end

function M.decodingIsUnchangedByTheSourceLength()
    -- One document at every offset a vector may start on, so the whole-vector
    -- path and the byte-at-a-time tail both cover every byte of it.
    for pad = 0, 65 do
        local text = string.rep(" ", pad) .. '{"a":[1,"b\\n",null,true],"c":{"d":-2.5}}'
        local mine, myError = decodedBy(fused, text)
        local theirs = decodedBy(lunajson, text)
        assert(myError == nil, string.format("padding by %d broke the decoder: %s", pad, tostring(myError)))
        assert(mine == theirs, string.format("padding by %d changed the value", pad))
    end
end

-- Sweep sparse Unicode transitions and short tails across vector boundaries.
-- A later malformed sequence must never displace the first error in the input.
function M.scanPreservesSparseUnicodeTransitionsAndFirstErrors()
    local euro, smile = "\226\130\172", "\240\159\152\128"
    for pad = 0, 260 do
        for _, gap in ipairs({0, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 65, 127, 128, 129}) do
            local text = '"' .. string.rep("a", pad) .. euro .. string.rep("b", gap) .. smile .. string.rep("c", pad % 67) .. '"'
            local mine, message = decodedBy(fused, text)
            local theirs, other = decodedBy(lunajson, text)
            assert(message == nil and other == nil, "mixed Unicode refused at " .. pad .. ":" .. gap .. ": " .. tostring(message))
            assert(mine == theirs, "mixed Unicode changed at " .. pad .. ":" .. gap)
        end
        for _, bad in ipairs(BAD_UTF8) do
            for _, suffix in ipairs({"", string.rep("z", 65)}) do
                local text = '"' .. string.rep("a", pad) .. bad .. suffix .. '"'
                local code, position = referenceScan(text)
                assert(code == INVALID_UTF8, "reference missed malformed UTF-8")
                local _, message = decodedBy(fused, text)
                local reported = message and tonumber(message:match("at byte (%d+)"))
                assert(reported == position, "malformed UTF-8 at " .. pad .. ": " .. tostring(reported) .. " vs " .. position)
            end
        end
        -- A control error before later malformed Unicode stays first.
        local text = '"' .. string.rep("a", pad) .. "\001" .. string.rep("b", 65) .. "\255\""
        local code, position = referenceScan(text)
        assert(code == INVALID_CONTROL)
        local _, message = decodedBy(fused, text)
        assert(message and tonumber(message:match("at byte (%d+)")) == position, "later Unicode displaced earlier control error")
    end
end

-- Exercise every byte class on both sides of the ASCII/Unicode transition,
-- with enough following bytes to cover full vectors as well as short tails.
function M.everyByteClassPreservesValuesAndFirstErrorsAcrossTransitions()
    for _, prefix in ipairs({"", "\226\130\172"}) do
        for pad = 0, 80 do
            for byte = 0, 255 do
                for _, tail in ipairs({"", string.rep("z", 17)}) do
                    local text = '"' .. prefix .. string.rep("a", pad) .. string.char(byte) .. tail .. '"'
                    local code, position = referenceScan(text)
                    local mine, message = decodedBy(fused, text)
                    local theirs, other = decodedBy(lunajson, text)
                    assert((message == nil) == (other == nil), "byte-class acceptance at " .. pad .. ":" .. byte)
                    if code ~= OK then
                        local reported = message and tonumber(message:match("at byte (%d+)"))
                        assert(reported == position, "byte-class error at " .. pad .. ":" .. byte .. ": " .. tostring(reported) .. " vs " .. position)
                    elseif message == nil then
                        assert(mine == theirs, "byte-class value at " .. pad .. ":" .. byte)
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    end
end

return M

from pathlib import Path
import json,math,statistics,sys
root=Path(sys.argv[1]); protocol=json.loads((root/'protocol.json').read_text()); n=protocol['forks_per_payload'];t={3:4.3026527299,25:2.0638985616}[n]
rows=[]
for payload in ('ascii','unicode','sparseUnicode'):
 forks=[json.loads(p.read_text()) for p in sorted(root.glob(payload+'-??.json'))]
 assert len(forks)==n,(payload,len(forks))
 data=[f['payloads'][0] for f in forks]; first=data[0]
 assert all(d['payload']==payload and d['digest']==first['digest'] and len(d['fused']['samples'])==protocol['samples_per_fork'] for d in data)
 paired=[statistics.median(math.log(a/b) for a,b in zip(d['fused']['samples'],d['baseline']['samples'])) for d in data]
 center=statistics.mean(paired); delta=t*statistics.stdev(paired)/math.sqrt(n)
 low,high=math.exp(center-delta),math.exp(center+delta)
 verdict='improved' if low>1/.99 else 'regressed' if high<1/1.01 else 'unchanged' if low>=1/1.01 and high<=1/.99 else 'inconclusive'
 control=[d['lunajson']['median'] for d in data]
 rows.append({'payload':payload,'bytes':first['bytes'],'digest':first['digest'],'forks':n,'candidate_MBps':statistics.median(d['fused']['median'] for d in data),'baseline_MBps':statistics.median(d['baseline']['median'] for d in data),'throughput_ratio':math.exp(center),'ratio_CI95':[low,high],'duration_change_percent':100*(1/math.exp(center)-1),'verdict':verdict,'control_MBps':statistics.median(control),'control_min_max':[min(control),max(control)],'control_cv_percent':100*statistics.stdev(control)/statistics.mean(control),'fork_paired_log_ratios':paired})
report={'payloads':rows,'retention_pass':rows[0]['ratio_CI95'][0]>1/.99 and all(row['ratio_CI95'][0]>1/1.01 for row in rows[1:])}
(root/'summary.json').write_text(json.dumps(report,indent=2)+'\n');print(json.dumps(report,indent=2))

from pathlib import Path
import subprocess, time, json, datetime, os, signal
out=Path('/private/tmp/nupp-63-qualified-processes.jsonl')
assert not out.exists()
blocked={'cargo','rustc','clang','clang++','cc1','cc','gcc','ninja','make','cmake','luajit'}
proc=None
with out.open('w') as log:
 def sample():
  rows=[]
  for line in subprocess.check_output(['ps','-Ao','pid,ppid,pcpu,comm'],text=True).splitlines()[1:]:
   x=line.split(None,3)
   if len(x)!=4: continue
   pid,ppid,cpu,command=int(x[0]),int(x[1]),float(x[2]),Path(x[3]).name
   own=False
   if proc is not None:
    try: own=os.getpgid(pid)==proc.pid
    except ProcessLookupError: pass
   if cpu>5 or command in blocked:
    rows.append(dict(pid=pid,ppid=ppid,cpu=cpu,command=command,measurement_process=own))
  bad=[r for r in rows if r['command'] in blocked and (r['command'] != 'luajit' or r['cpu'] > 5) and not r['measurement_process']]
  log.write(json.dumps(dict(utc=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(),phase='measurement' if proc else 'quiet_guard',processes=rows,compiler_interference=bool(bad)))+'\n');log.flush()
  return bad
 for i in range(15):
  bad=sample()
  if bad: raise SystemExit('No qualification started: external build process present: '+repr(bad))
  time.sleep(1)
 with open('/private/tmp/nupp-63-events-carry-qualified-formal-run.log','w') as runlog:
  proc=subprocess.Popen(['python3','/private/tmp/nupp-63-events-carry-qualified-measure.py','formal'],stdout=runlog,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,start_new_session=True)
  contaminated=False
  while proc.poll() is None:
   if sample(): contaminated=True
   time.sleep(.5)
  # Preserve every fork even when an external job invalidates the environment.
  code=proc.returncode
  Path('/private/tmp/nupp-63-qualified-environment.json').write_text(json.dumps(dict(complete=code==0,compiler_interference=contaminated,qualified=code==0 and not contaminated),indent=2)+'\n')
  if code or contaminated: raise SystemExit('Qualification invalidated; all observations preserved.')
print('Complete environment-qualified run; numerical analysis still required.')
